**Remaining Enrolled After Moving to Texas**

- If your student moves to Texas, he can remain enrolled in Texas Tech K-12 as a full-time student.
- You may also apply to switch from the tuition-paid (international) program to the tuition-free Texas resident program if you meet eligibility requirements.

---

**Switching to the Tuition-Free Resident Program**

To switch to the tuition-free program, the following conditions must be met:
- **Texas Residency:** The student must be a Texas resident under the age of 25.
- **Proof of Residency:** You must provide documentation showing a Texas residential address (e.g., current deed, lease, mortgage statement, utility bill, military documents, or a letter from the Texas Juvenile Justice Department).
- **Withdrawal from Local School:** The student must withdraw from any local Texas public school to enroll full-time in the tuition-free program.
- **Enrollment Requirements:** The student must be scheduled into at least four semester courses and maintain satisfactory course progress.
- **State Testing:** The student will be required to participate in all mandatory State of Texas Assessments of Academic Readiness (STAAR) and End-of-Course (EOC) exams for their grade level.

**Application Process:**
- Submit a new application for the tuition-free program and provide all required Texas residency documentation.
- Admission is subject to available space and, if applicable, the lottery process for tuition-free enrollment.

---

**Transferring to Another Texas Public High School**

If your student transfers to another Texas public high school, Texas Tech K-12 will provide:
- **Official Transcript:** An official transcript showing all completed courses, grades, and credits earned through Texas Tech K-12.
- **Course Records:** The transcript will include the student’s grade level, course titles, final grades, and credits awarded.
- **Additional Documentation:** Upon request, Texas Tech K-12 can provide course descriptions or syllabi if the receiving school requires them for credit evaluation.

**How to Request Records:**
- Official transcripts can be requested through the Texas Tech K-12 portal or by submitting a [High School Transcript Request Form](https://appserv.itts.ttu.edu/TTUISDWebForms/HighSchoolTranscriptRequest/Form).

---

- For questions about switching programs or requesting transcripts, contact TTU K-12 at 1-800-692-6877 or ttuk12@ttu.edu.

**Texas Public High School Diploma and Transcript**

- The Texas Tech K-12 full-time diploma program issues an official Texas public high school diploma.
- The diploma and transcript are fully accredited by the Texas Education Agency (TEA) and are suitable for freshman applications to Texas public universities.
- The official transcript includes all completed courses, grades, and credits, and is recognized by Texas public universities and colleges.

---

**GPA and Class Rank Reporting**

- **GPA Calculation:** Texas Tech K-12 calculates a student’s final GPA using all eligible coursework that applies toward high school graduation, including transferred credits from accredited schools (unless designated as local credit or pass/fail).
- **Weighted GPA:** Advanced Placement (AP), Honors, International Baccalaureate (IB), and Dual Credit courses receive additional GPA weight.
- **Class Rank:**  
  - Texas Tech K-12 does **not** calculate or report class rank except for students in the Top 10% of a given class, as required by Texas law.
  - Class rank will not appear on transcripts except for Top 10% students.
  - Students in the Top 10% will be notified of their status and the GPA cut point for Top 10% is communicated to all students in each class in January and June of the sophomore, junior, and senior year.

---

**College Counseling and Support**

- **Academic Advisors:** Full-time students are assigned academic advisors who assist with graduation planning, course selection, and college readiness.
- **College Application Support:** Advisors and teachers provide recommendation letters for college and scholarship applications (request at least two weeks in advance).
- **Fast-Track Admissions:** Texas Tech K-12 graduates are eligible for a fast-track admissions process to Texas Tech University.
- **Scholarship Guidance:** Information and support are available for applying to Texas Tech K-12 exclusive scholarships and external opportunities.
- **Transcript Requests:** Advisors assist with official transcript requests for college applications.

---

**Summary**

- Graduates receive an official, accredited Texas public high school diploma and transcript suitable for Texas public university freshman applications.
- GPA is reported; class rank is only reported for Top 10% as required by law.
- College counseling, academic advising, and application support are available to all full-time students.

**For more information or personalized support, contact TTU K-12 at 1-800-692-6877 or ttuk12@ttu.edu.**

**Overview of Texas Tech K-12**

Texas Tech K-12 is an accredited, flexible online school program operated by Texas Tech University. It serves students from kindergarten through 12th grade and offers a variety of enrollment options to meet diverse educational needs. Texas Tech K-12 is designed for students who require an alternative to traditional schooling, such as those who travel frequently, have health issues, are pursuing athletics or arts, or need a non-traditional academic schedule.

**Key Features**

- **Fully Accredited**: Accredited by the Texas Education Agency (TEA) and Cognia.
- **Flexible, Self-Paced Learning**: Courses are asynchronous, allowing students to enroll at any time and work at their own pace.
- **Comprehensive Curriculum**: Offers core subjects, electives, Advanced Placement (AP) courses, and dual credit opportunities.
- **Multiple Enrollment Options**:
  - Full-Time Diploma Programs (Tuition-Free for eligible Texas residents, or Tuition-Paid for others)
  - Supplemental/Part-Time Courses (for students enrolled elsewhere)
  - Credit by Exam (CBE) for acceleration or credit recovery
  - College Preparatory Academy (structured dual credit pathway)
- **Global Reach**: Available to students across Texas, the United States, and internationally.
- **Support for Special Populations**: Accommodations for students with disabilities, military families, and gifted/talented learners.

**Who Can Benefit?**

- Students needing a flexible or alternative school schedule
- Homeschoolers seeking accredited coursework
- Students wanting to accelerate or recover credits
- Military families, international students, and those with unique educational needs
